scenes.heading: Letter series and codes
scenes.sub: Turn letters into numbers and the pattern appears
scenes.say: C, F, I, L… what comes next? Letter puzzles look scary, but there's a simple trick: turn the letters into numbers. Then the pattern jumps out.

scenes.heading: Think of it like this
scenes.science: Each letter has a number: A is 1, Z is 26
scenes.breaks: A street just ends. The alphabet can wrap round, so after Z comes A again.
scenes.say: Think of the alphabet as a street with twenty-six houses. A lives at number one and Z at number twenty-six. To move along the street, you add or take away. The difference is that the alphabet can wrap round, so after Z you're back at A.

scenes.heading: Landmarks to remember
points: A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, C ↔ X
scenes.caption: E = 5, J = 10, O = 15, T = 20, Y = 25. Mirror partners add to 27: A ↔ Z, B ↔ Y, C ↔ X.
scenes.say: Learn these landmarks: E is five, J is ten, O is fifteen, T is twenty, Y is twenty-five. Jump to the nearest one and count from there. And in a mirror code, A swaps with Z, B with Y, and partners always add to twenty-seven.

scenes.heading: Cracking a series
steps: Continue, then turn back to letters
scenes.say: To crack a series, change the letters to numbers and write the gaps. If the gaps look random, split it into two series. Continue the pattern, then turn the number back into a letter.

scenes.heading: Two series mixed together
scenes.question: What comes next? B, Y, D, W, F, U, ___
scenes.say: B, Y, D, W, F, U. The gaps are wild, so split it. The odd places go B, D, F, up two. The even places go Y, W, U, down two. Place seven is odd, so it's F plus two, which is H.

scenes.heading: Decoding
scenes.question: MOVE is written NPWF. Which word is written SBJO?
lines: S → R, B → A, J → I, O → N
scenes.say: MOVE is written N P W F, so each letter moves forward one. To decode S B J O, go the other way: back one. S becomes R, B becomes A, J becomes I, and O becomes N. The word is RAIN.

Recap. Turn letters into numbers, and write the gaps before you guess. If the gaps are weird, split the series. And to decode, reverse the code, then check by coding it again. Now try the practice questions!
